statusText: Tail eases to 11%. Mapped policy state: EA_ON. A third Globex hour leaves the overnight band unchanged and the Nikkei has lifted off its session low, while Stress holds at 49% on firmer crude and multi-decade-high long-end yields.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with Tail in the low band and below the block threshold. The narrow danger window spans the 13:30Z US cash open through 15:00Z, where an opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the first meaningful Tail evidence. The 17:00Z 30-Year Bond Auction, with the 30Y near its highest since May 2002, is the clearest delayed-second-leg mechanism later in the window. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold an unchanged overnight band for a third hour as Asian cash lifts off its low
body: Three Globex hours are now observed and the overnight band is unchanged at 31,372.25-31,459.00. NQ Dec26 trades 31,442.50, +0.13% against a 31,402.25 prior close, having moved from mid-range last hour into the upper third without taking out the 31,459.00 high. Neither band edge extended, so a third consecutive hour shows rotation with no directional efficiency, no repeated extension and no failed retracement. That remains the central Tail-negative observation, reinforced by the Oct 7 cash session: the Nasdaq-100 closed 31,160.08, -0.21%, after a dip to 30,904.46 was fully retraced into a close just 10 points under the 31,170.12 high. The new development this hour is that Asian cash is mean-reverting rather than cascading. The Nikkei 225 trades 69,350.27, -0.98%, recovered about 155 points from its 69,195.47 session low against a 70,035.71 prior close, an improvement on the -1.11% print near the low an hour ago. Hong Kong has reopened at 24,081.69, -0.20%, mid-range inside 24,031.66-24,146.01. Asian equities are therefore softer but orderly, and the divergence from NQ stays mild. The macro backdrop remains more stressed than the price path. The September 15-16 FOMC minutes, released Oct 7, show most participants judging that another increase in the federal funds target range would likely be appropriate by year end, with the range now 3.75-4.00 percent. The 10Y closed at 5.28 percent after reaching 5.36 percent intraday, its highest since April 2002, and the 30Y closed at 5.66 percent after 5.73 percent, its highest since May 2002; both pulled back from their highs, which is itself a sign of orderly rather than discontinuous repricing. H.15 carries the 2Y at 4.79 percent for Oct 6. VIX settled at 15.08 after a 16.01 intraday print, a low absolute level. Crude continues to firm, with Brent at 101.92, +1.71 percent, and WTI at 89.64, +1.54 percent, against reported attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and a Gulf storm threat to offshore production. Under the repository contract this combination of hawkish repricing, firm crude and softer Asian cash informs Stress and Confidence rather than Tail, because no persistent one-way NQ structure, shallow-pullback sequence or repeated extension after a failed retracement has been observed. Tail therefore eases to 11 percent with Stress held at 49 percent. The shared Finviz context file is dated Sep 29 with partial collection status, roughly nine days stale, so it was not used as current evidence; research for this run was independent and primary-source based.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 10-14% through the Asian and European hours of Oct 7, rose to a 20-23% WATCH band between 11:00Z and 15:00Z as a trend-down phase developed into the US open, then decayed steadily to 11-18% once the dip to 30,904.46 was fully retraced into the cash close. Stress held a 45-54% elevated band and Confidence stayed in the high band at 87-89%.
outlookSummary: Base case is continued two-way NQ rotation while multi-decade-high long-end yields, firm crude and softer but orderly Asian cash remain the dominant background conflict. Conditional Tail holds 11-12% through the Asian hours, rises to 13-17% across the European session and the 08:30Z Waller speech, reaches a 21% peak across the 12:30Z claims block and the 13:30Z US cash open, eases to 18-19% late morning, returns to 20% for the 17:00Z 30-Year Bond Auction, then decays to 11-15% after the 20:00Z cash close. Stress tracks 46-56% with peaks at the open and the auction. The 30-Year auction with the long end near its 2002 highs is the clearest credible delayed-second-leg mechanism in the window.
